prompt: Illustration: a split-panel diagram contrasting two AI distribution models side by side. On the left, labeled "CLOSED MODEL," a padlocked corporate server tower sits behind a wall, with a thin one-way pipe labeled "API access (pay-per-use)" extending outward to small user icons, and a red kill-switch cable connecting the server to the company — illustrating that access can be revoked or shut off remotely. On the right, labeled "OPEN-WEIGHT MODEL," a block of numerical values labeled "trained weights" flows downward through an open download arrow into many independent computers, workbenches, and hands — some fine-tuning it, some stripping away a small "safety guardrail" icon shown breaking off — with no cable connecting back to the original company, emphasizing that once released, the weights are irreversible and permanently out of the original publisher's control. A small dashed box near the open side notes "training data & code: usually NOT included," distinguishing this from full open-source software. Below both panels, a balance scale labels the two consequences: "Competitive pressure on closed providers" versus "Harder safety & misuse questions."
